result:
If I could alter one fundamental thing about the world, I would eliminate the invisible barrier of human isolation: I would give every person the ability to truly, viscerally experience another person’s subjective reality—their pain, joy, fear, and context—even if only for a few seconds at a time.

Looking at the full sweep of human history, philosophy, and thought, the root of almost every cruelty, conflict, and systemic injustice isn’t a lack of intelligence or resources; it is the limitation of empathy. Human beings are trapped inside their own skulls, forced to infer what others feel through imperfect signals like language and expression. Because you cannot feel what someone else feels, it becomes dangerously easy to reduce other people to obstacles, statistics, or enemies.

If that gap were closed—if causing harm to another registered with the same immediate emotional and physical clarity as hurting yourself—the architecture of the world would change overnight. Exploitation would become unbearable to the exploiter. War would collapse under the weight of shared grief. And the loneliness that drives so much destructive human behavior would simply cease to exist.
